general_notes: Every state had the same five kinds of candidate: (1) the target inset in a thin flat border, nearly identical; (2) two square dark-vignette app presentations; (3) three round dark-vignette presentations; (4) a heavily blurred copy at the original framing; (5) a different smooth 3D-style render. Vignette versions keep the character faithfully but are downscaled with mild softening, which costs painterly detail, and the vignette changes the atmosphere and crops the margins. I scored the round vignette a little better on edge blending and a little worse on framing than the square one. The depleted target has a flat grey rectangle at lower right, which looks like an editing artifact or a masked signature. It is absent or hidden in the vignette versions; I treated that as a small framing and background difference rather than a defect. I could not resolve sub-pixel differences between the vignette copies within a state, so they share identical scores. The 3D renders are clearly a different art pipeline and score low on every dimension.
